headline: Inner Canyon Permits and Rim Campground Bookings
reservation: General entry does not currently require a timed permit, but all inner-canyon hiking requires a wilderness permit obtained on-site. South Rim campsites require reservations; North Rim campsites are first-come, first-served, with payment through Recreation.gov Scan & Pay. Systems are subject to change, so verify current status on the official NPS site before arrival.

days.title: South Rim Verticality

stops.name: Pulpit Rock Overlook
stops.detail: Experience the canyon's sheer depth at one of the most accessible and dramatic viewpoints on the South Rim.

stops.name: Painted Wall View
stops.detail: Observe the highest cliff in Colorado, famous for the intricate pink pegmatite dikes etched into the dark rock.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the scenic rim drive; conditions vary.
days.note: The South Rim Drive is paved but narrow; avoid stopping on the roadway.

days.title: River Depths and Grade

stops.name: East Portal Road
stops.detail: Descend to the Gunnison River via a 16% grade road to feel the power of the water at the canyon floor.

stops.name: Gunnison Point
stops.detail: Visit the main visitor center area for geological exhibits and a view of the canyon's narrowest sections.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; the descent is extremely slow and steep.
days.note: Vehicles over 22 feet are prohibited on East Portal Road due to hairpin turns.

days.title: The Remote North Rim

stops.name: Exclamation Point
stops.detail: Hike the North Vista Trail for a panoramic perspective of the canyon that most visitors never see.

stops.name: Chasm View
stops.detail: Peer down to the river at its most turbulent and narrow point from the rugged North Rim edge.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours to transit between rims; conditions vary.
days.note: The North Rim is accessed via unpaved roads and is closed during winter months.

intel.title: Overlook Limits
intel.text: Small lots at Sunset View and Pulpit Rock fill by 10 AM during summer months. Arrive before 9 AM to ensure access to the most popular South Rim vistas.

intel.title: Canyon Blackouts
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent within the canyon and highly unreliable on the North Rim. Use the South Rim Visitor Center for any necessary digital communications.

intel.title: Montrose Hub
intel.text: Fuel up in Montrose or Gunnison before entering the park; no gas is available within park boundaries. The North Rim has no services nearby other than small shops in Crawford.

intel.title: Inner Canyon Heat
intel.text: Temps on the canyon floor can exceed 100 degrees in July while the rim remains temperate. Plan any descent for early morning to avoid peak heat and afternoon storms.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: South Rim Road beyond Gunnison Point and the entire North Rim Road close following the first significant snow, usually by November. Access is limited to snowshoes or skis.

plan.arrival: Fly into Montrose Regional Airport (MTJ) and drive 20 minutes to Montrose for supplies before heading to the South Rim entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for the South Rim, but heavy-duty brakes are essential for East Portal Road; check RV length limits.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset View on the South Rim provides the best perspective as the canyon walls glow in late-season light.
